title: Japan national CPI (August 2026) — decision-day morning in Tokyo, and the BoJ ledger's own data kill switch
source: EST: stat.go.jp/english/data/cpi/1582.html ('Consumer Price Index — Schedule of Release'), re-fetched direct 2026-09-15 (HTTP 200, 13,839 bytes) and parsed cell-by-cell out of its single 17-row HTML table by this session, independently of the fetch that seeded the proposal this file supersedes. Against the header pair ['Japan: Survey month | Date of release', 'Ku-area of Tokyo (preliminary): Survey month | Date of release', 'Remarks'] the row parses exactly as ['August', 'September 18', 'September', 'October 2', ''] — i.e. the August-2026 NATIONAL CPI releases 2026-09-18 (a Friday), with an empty Remarks cell, so this release carries no yearly or fiscal-yearly average. The column pairing is corroborated by the adjacent rows reproducing the independent parses recorded in japan-cpi-2026-11-20.json ('October','November 20') and japan-cpi-2026-12-18 ('November','December 18'). Filed estimate on three counts, identical to every sibling Japanese entry: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has BLS:/BEA:/CENSUS: for US statistical agencies and no slot for Japan's Statistics Bureau, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and the schedule page's own stamp is still 'Last Update : 23 January 2026'. The 08:30 JST release time is NOT read off this page and is not asserted here — this session attempted stat.go.jp/english/data/cpi/index.html (HTTP 200, 11,714 B) and stat.go.jp/data/cpi/sokuhou/tsuki/index-z.html (HTTP 200, 13,875 B) and neither states a publication time; it is registered as a scoreable forward test instead of carried as a caption.
notes: CANONICAL entry written 2026-09-15 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, superseding proposals/japan-cpi-2026-09-18.from-boj-decision-2026-09-18.json (read first, per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md; it stays where it is and is now shadowed). The proposer's reason holds and this session sharpened it: this print is the boj-decision-2026-09-18 ledger's registered DATA KILL SWITCH — 'Japanese national core CPI printing at or above 2.0% before the decision' — and it lands on the morning of the decision itself. What the initial research adds is the arithmetic that switch turns on. National core (less fresh food, weight 9621, 2025-base) was index 102.1 in July 2026 against 100.3 in August 2025; the published y/y therefore steps in ~0.098pp increments, and 2.0% requires the index to print 102.3 or higher, i.e. a Jul->Aug core m/m of at least +0.196%. The 2013-2025 national August seasonal is +0.117% (sd 0.173) and the 2000-2025 seasonal is +0.116% (sd 0.136), both BELOW the trigger — but replaying each of the 26 historical August m/m moves onto 102.1 puts the print at or above 2.0% in 10 of 26 cases. So another ledger's kill switch is a near-coin-flip decided by one index tick, and the modal published outcome (+1.8%, 9 of 26) sits two ticks under it. Impact stays LOW for the reasons every Japanese macro entry on this calendar carries: symbols is empty, no house playbook is keyed to Japanese CPI, and the channel to this book's AI names runs through yen funding and global term premium, both second-order and both already owned by the FOMC ledgers. The 2026-09-18 US session is separately and heavily confounded — it is a $6.2T triple-witching (opex-2026-09-18, confirmed, high) two days after the FOMC (fomc-2026-09-16, confirmed, high) — so nothing in that tape is attributable to a Tokyo print without ruling both out first. One caveat the proposal recorded as unresolved is now settled: the schedule page's Remarks column dates the 2025-base revision to the JULY-data release (2026-08-21), so the 2026-09-18 print is the second release on the new base, and this session's own parse of the Bureau's national file shows a continuous 2025=100 series 1970-01 -> 2026-07 with no splice inside it.
